hero: Convert mouse sensitivity between Fortnite, Valorant, CS2, Apex, and more using cm/360. Treat the result as a starting point — FOV and ADS settings still differ per game.

seo.s1h: How to use this Fortnite sensitivity calculator
seo.s1p1: Enter the DPI from your mouse software (Logitech G Hub, Razer Synapse, etc.), pick the game you already play, type that game's sensitivity, and convert to Fortnite. The output is a Fortnite X/Y starting value that keeps the same physical cm/360 turn distance.
seo.s1p2: After converting, open Fortnite to Settings to Mouse and Keyboard, paste the result into Sensitivity X and Sensitivity Y, then spend 10-15 minutes in a Creative aim / edit map before judging it in pubs or Ranked.
seo.s2h: Valorant, CS2, and Apex to Fortnite (what transfers)
seo.s2p1: Players switching from Valorant, CS2, or Apex usually want the same muscle memory for tracking and flicks. Matching cm/360 gets hipfire close. What does not transfer 1:1: scoped/ADS multipliers, Fortnite's build camera, edit speed, and faster camera work for piece control than in a pure tac shooter.
seo.s2p2: If builds feel sticky after a Valorant convert, raise Fortnite sens a little (or keep hipfire and only raise building/edit multipliers if you use separate values). If sprays feel shaky, drop slightly and widen your mousepad clearance for 180s.
seo.s3h: Fortnite eDPI and common 800 DPI ranges
seo.s3p1: eDPI = in-game sensitivity x mouse DPI. It lets you compare settings across DPI choices. Example: 0.08 sens at 800 DPI = 64 eDPI; 0.04 sens at 1600 DPI is also 64 eDPI and the same cm/360 if the game scale matches.
seo.s3p2: At 800 DPI, a practical Fortnite starting band is roughly 0.05-0.08 for steadier mid-range fights, 0.12-0.18 for very fast build/edit playstyles, and ~0.07-0.10 for many competitive KBM players. Use the calculator's eDPI readout to sanity-check — Fortnite eDPI in the tens of thousands usually means the wrong game multiplier or a decimal typo.
seo.s4h: After you convert — fine-tune in Creative
seo.s4p1: Do a few 180s, track a strafing bot, and run a short edit course. Ask: can I do a full turn without lifting twice? Can I micro-correct sprays without jitter? If not, nudge sens by ~5-10% and retest. Small changes beat jumping from 0.06 to 0.15 in one night.
seo.s4p2: Keep DPI fixed while you tune Fortnite sens. Changing both at once makes it hard to know what fixed the feel. Pair sens work with stable FPS — see our FPS settings guide if frame time spikes make aim feel like bad sens.

faqs.q1: Will converted sensitivity feel identical in Fortnite?
faqs.a1: cm/360 matching is the closest hipfire feel transfer between games, but Fortnite's FOV, building, editing, and scoped sensitivities still feel different. Treat the result as a Creative warmup starting point, then nudge X/Y until tracking and 180s feel natural.
faqs.q2: What eDPI range do Fortnite mouse players use?
faqs.a2: Many KBM players land roughly in the 40-100 eDPI range (sensitivity x DPI). A common competitive band at 800 DPI is about 0.07-0.10 sens (eDPI ~56-80). There is no single pro value — comfort and consistency matter more.
faqs.q3: How do I convert Valorant sensitivity to Fortnite?
faqs.a3: Enter your Valorant sens and mouse DPI, set Convert From to Valorant and Convert To to Fortnite, then hit Convert. The tool matches cm/360 so a full turn uses the same mouse distance. Apply the Fortnite number in Settings to Mouse and Keyboard to Sensitivity X/Y.
faqs.q4: How do I convert CS2 or Apex sensitivity to Fortnite?
faqs.a4: Same flow: pick CS2 / CS:GO or Apex Legends as the source game, enter sens + DPI, convert to Fortnite. Apex and CS2 share a similar yaw scale in many converters; always keep DPI identical on both sides of the conversion.
faqs.q5: What is cm/360 and why does this calculator use it?
faqs.a5: cm/360 is how many centimeters your mouse moves for a full 360 degree turn. Games use different raw sensitivity scales, so matching cm/360 is the standard way to transfer hipfire feel instead of copying the same decimal number between titles.
faqs.q6: Should my Fortnite X and Y sensitivity be the same?
faqs.a6: Most players start with matching X and Y after a conversion. Some raise Y slightly for builds and edits. If you change one axis, re-test tracking in Creative before ranked.
faqs.q7: Does this work for controller sensitivity?
faqs.a7: No — this converter is for mouse DPI + in-game mouse sensitivity. Controller look speed, deadzones, and aim assist curves are a different system. Use in-game controller settings or Creative testing instead.
